title: Coastal Regulation Zone, Mangroves and Blue Carbon

cards.b:
The coast faces cyclones, sea-level rise and building pressure. Prelims asks about CRZ categories, mangrove species and sites, and blue carbon. Mains asks if CRZ relaxations help or harm.

Mangroves also feature in climate questions as cheap protection.

Expect a question that pairs a CRZ category with its description.

The Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) Notification was first issued in 1991 under the Environment (Protection) Act 1986. It was revised in 2011 and replaced by the CRZ Notification 2019. CRZ covers the land up to 500 metres from the High Tide Line (HTL) on the sea side, the land along tidal-influenced water bodies, and the waters up to 12 nautical miles seaward.

The National Coastal Zone Management Authority and State authorities enforce it. A separate Island Protection Zone notification (2011) covers Andaman and Nicobar and Lakshadweep.

• CRZ-I: ecologically sensitive areas (mangroves, corals, turtle nesting grounds, salt marshes) and the intertidal zone. Little or no building.
  • CRZ-II: urban shoreline already built up. Construction allowed on the landward side of the existing road.
  • CRZ-III: rural and undeveloped coast. A no-development zone of 200 m from the HTL; densely populated rural areas (CRZ-IIIA) have 50 m after 2019.
  • CRZ-IV: water area from low tide line to 12 nautical miles, plus tidal water bodies. Fishing allowed, no solid waste dumping.

The 2019 rules allow some tourism facilities and use floor space index relaxation in urban areas.

Mangroves grow in tidal mud in the tropics. They have pneumatophores (breathing roots), prop roots and vivipary (seeds sprout on the tree). Species: Rhizophora, Avicennia, and Heritiera fomes (Sundari, which gave the Sundarbans its name).

India has about 4,990 sq km of mangroves (ISFR 2021, roughly 0.15 percent of land). West Bengal has the largest share (Sundarbans), followed by Gujarat and Andaman and Nicobar. Bhitarkanika in Odisha has the saltwater crocodile and Olive Ridley nesting nearby. Mangroves cushion cyclones and tsunamis, trap sediment, and serve as fish nurseries.

Blue carbon is carbon stored by coastal and marine ecosystems: mangroves, seagrass meadows and salt marshes. They store carbon in the soil for centuries, often more per hectare than land forests. Draining or clearing them releases it.

The Blue Carbon Initiative is run by Conservation International, IUCN and UNESCO IOC. India started a MISHTI scheme (Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats and Tangible Incomes) in 2023 and has launched blue carbon projects in the Sundarbans and Odisha. Blue carbon is also a topic for carbon markets and NDCs.

Aquaculture ponds (shrimp farms), ports, tourism, sand mining, and sea-level rise eat into mangroves. Coral and seagrass beds suffer from trawling and bleaching. Mumbai and Kerala lost large mangrove areas to land reclamation.

The Supreme Court's S. Jagannath v Union of India (1996) is the standard case: it banned intensive shrimp farming inside the CRZ. The Bombay High Court (2018) ordered strong protection of mangroves.

Coral reefs in India are at the Gulf of Mannar, Palk Bay, Lakshadweep, Andaman and Nicobar, and the Gulf of Kutch. They are protected as Schedule I animals under the WPA, and corals need clear, warm, shallow water. Bleaching happens when stress makes corals expel their symbiotic algae (zooxanthellae). Seagrass meadows feed dugongs, which are Schedule I and live in the Gulf of Mannar, Palk Bay and Andaman waters. The Gulf of Kutch and Gulf of Mannar marine national parks (both 1982) were among India's first.

CRZ 2019 gave the states more say and cut the no-development zone in some areas, which supporters say helps fishers and ports. Critics say it weakens defences against cyclones. The Swaminathan Committee (2005) and Shailesh Nayak Committee (2014) shaped these rules.

A balanced answer: protect sensitive ecosystems fully, allow livelihoods for traditional fishers, and plan for sea-level rise.

Odisha's cyclone losses fell after better warning and shelters, and mangrove belts add a green shield. After the 2004 tsunami, studies noted that villages behind mangroves in Tamil Nadu fared better. Fishing communities want rights over the shore, and the Kerala coast sees erosion from sea walls and ports.

Prelims-style: "CRZ-III is" (rural, undeveloped, 200 m no-development zone). "Sundarbans is dominated by which mangrove tree?" (Sundari).

Mains-style: "Discuss the role of mangroves in coastal protection and climate mitigation. Do CRZ rules protect them?" Structure: functions; blue carbon; CRZ categories; threats; relaxations; way forward (MISHTI, local participation).
